key_insight: Pretraining codec-based avatar models at very large scale (mixing studio multi-view and millions of in-the-wild samples) produces representations that simultaneously achieve high-fidelity studio-level detail and strong generalization to real-world data.
problem_solved: Addresses the fidelity vs. generalization trade-off in 3D avatar modeling: studio multi-view captures deliver high detail but fail to generalize, while in-the-wild datasets generalize but lack fidelity. The paper shows large-scale pretraining can reconcile both.
method: Pretrain a codec-avatar model on a massive, heterogeneous dataset combining multi-view studio captures and millions of in-the-wild samples to learn a compact, expressive latent representation.

Use reconstruction- and representation-learning objectives (plus domain-bridging fine-tuning) so the pretrained avatar model preserves studio-level control while adapting to real-world appearance and pose variation.
Transfer the pretrained model to downstream tasks (high-fidelity rendering, expression/pose control, personalization) with light fine-tuning to achieve studio-quality results in the wild.
impact: Makes it practical to build photorealistic, controllable avatars that work outside controlled studios, reducing dependence on expensive capture rigs and accelerating applications in telepresence, AR/VR, and personalized content creation.

paper_title: Large-scale Codec Avatars: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Large-scale Avatar Pretraining
paper_authors: Junxuan Li, Rawal Khirodkar, Chengan He, Zhongshi Jiang, Giljoo Nam
